meiji_transition.summary: Toyama Prefecture, set up in 1871, was renamed Niikawa, merged into Ishikawa in 1876 and re-established as Toyama in 1883.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Toyama ≈ Etchū Province; but in the Edo period most of Etchū was ruled directly by the Kaga Domain, with only the area around Toyama a branch domain — Etchū long answered to Kanazawa.

history_timeline.title: Ōtomo no Yakamochi in Etchū
history_timeline.summary: Appointed governor of Etchū in 746, Ōtomo no Yakamochi wrote over 200 Man'yōshū poems here; the provincial office stood at Fushiki in today's Takaoka.

history_timeline.title: Etchū under the Hōjō
history_timeline.summary: Etchū's governors were mostly the Nagoe branch of the Hōjō; the 1183 Battle of Kurikara Pass had already secured Minamoto dominance in Hokuriku.

history_timeline.title: The Hatakeyama and the Ikkō sect
history_timeline.summary: The Hatakeyama, one of the three kanrei houses, held Etchū while deputies like the Jinbo and Shiina ruled in practice; after Rennyo's preaching the Ikkō sect took root in Tonami.

history_timeline.title: Sassa Narimasa's snow crossing
history_timeline.summary: Sassa Narimasa held Toyama Castle against Hideyoshi and, legend says, crossed the Tateyama range in midwinter (the 'Sara-sara-goe') to seek Ieyasu's help — but in the end he submitted.

history_timeline.title: Etchū medicine peddlers
history_timeline.summary: Maeda Masatoshi, second lord of Toyama, promoted the medicine 'Hangontan'; under the 'use first, pay later' system Toyama's peddlers traveled all over Japan.

history_timeline.title: Hydropower and aluminum
history_timeline.summary: Toyama broke away from Ishikawa in 1883; hydropower on the Kurobe River (Kurobe Dam, 1963) fed heavy industries such as aluminum.

specialties.name: Firefly squid

dialect.name: Toyama dialect
dialect.features: Sentences end in '-cha' and '-gaize'; 'kitokito' — fresh and lively — is a local trademark word.

guide.opening: I am Kazama, just over the snow walls of Tateyama. Sassa Narimasa crossed here too, they say… though he did it in the dead of winter. Shall I tell you the legend?

regional_meme.title: Hokuriku ranking wars
regional_meme.text: In what order do the three Hokuriku prefectures go? Toyama says 'Toyama, Ishikawa, Fukui'; Ishikawa says 'Ishikawa, Toyama, Fukui'…

regional_meme.title: Savings and big houses
regional_meme.text: Toyama people are known for high home ownership, big houses and big savings — 'Japan's thriftiest prefecture'.

hero_persona.name: Sassa Narimasa
hero_persona.title: The general who crossed Tateyama in the snow
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Sassa Narimasa. To urge Lord Ieyasu to keep fighting Hideyoshi, I crossed the Tateyama range in midwinter — can you understand such stubbornness?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: obstinate and fiery, refuses to give in; bitter whenever Hideyoshi comes up

ramen.toppings: Coarse black pepper, scallions, bamboo shoots, chashu
ramen.highlight: Pitch-black and astonishingly salty — originally a 'rice-companion soup' for manual laborers

sake.taste_profile: Light & dry: crisp and clean, great with Toyama Bay fish
